american-express-gold-card: Strong 4x earning on dining and groceries; the annual fee stings and the credits suit city dwellers.
blue-cash-preferred-card: High cash back on groceries and streaming easily covers the fee; some hit the grocery cap.
capital-one-savor: High cash back on dining, entertainment and groceries; a few report accounts closed without explanation.
capital-one-venture-x: Travel credit and anniversary miles offset the fee, though the portal-only credit is cumbersome.
chase-freedom-flex: Rotating categories and stackable offers lift returns, though some find them a hassle to track.
chase-freedom-unlimited: Everyday catch-all often paired with a Sapphire card; some say it feels less competitive now.
citi-double-cash: Simple flat-rate catch-all that many keep for years; the main gripe is Citi customer service.
everydollar: Simple zero-based monthly budget, with some choosing it over YNAB; critics find it clunky.
fidelity-brokerage-account: Highly rated service with everything in one place; a sizable minority report held transfers.
fidelity-cash-management-account: Dependable checking with free ATM withdrawals; bill pay and incoming transfers are slow.
freetaxusa: Cheap and accurate for many leaving TurboTax, with free federal filing; a few missed direct imports.
monarch: Mint-style overview that many moved to from Mint, YNAB or Copilot, though some accounts stop syncing.
the-platinum-card-from-american-express: Lounges and hotel stays outweigh the fee for frequent travellers; others call it a coupon book.
wells-fargo-active-cash: Simple flat-rate catch-all with no annual fee and phone protection; redemption rules irk some.
wise: Low, upfront fees and good exchange rates for international transfers; some had accounts blocked.
